sketches.title: Return to Sender
sketches.premise: Two rival postal clerks fight over one package. Each turn, stamp a new standing postal problem that defeats the problem before it: what you are must act on what stands, not merely avoid it. The judge decides whether your mailroom solution actually overcomes the previous one.
sketches.criterion: A move beats what stands by opening, redirecting, delivering, canceling, exposing, or otherwise stopping its postal effect; dodging it, surviving it, making a bigger copy, or naming a cousin from the same postal family does not count.
sketches.move_shape: Say what postal thing you are and what it does to the previous thing: “I am a return label; I send the lost package back to the wrong address.”
sketches.first_card: I am an undeliverable package, bloated with mystery and bad handwriting.

sketches.title: Sorting Room Showdown
sketches.premise: The mail has become a chain of mistakes, and two sorters must correct it one error at a time. On every turn, name a standing postal item or instruction that fixes the one before it; the judge rules whether the correction really works.
sketches.criterion: A move beats the standing item by directly correcting, separating, rerouting, sealing, or making its mistake impossible; merely hiding, ignoring, outlasting, or enlarging the same mistake loses.
sketches.move_shape: Name your postal thing and its correction: “I am a zip code; I force this address into the right street.”
sketches.first_card: I am a letter addressed only to ‘that blue house near the big tree.’

sketches.title: Fragile: Handle With Drama
sketches.premise: A package travels through a catastrophically theatrical post office. Each turn, become one standing hazard or protection that acts on the previous one, either causing or preventing a postal disaster. The judge decides whether the new item genuinely defeats what stands.
sketches.criterion: A move beats the standing postal thing by breaking, blocking, containing, labeling, redirecting, or safely neutralizing its effect; simply enduring it, stepping aside, using a bigger version, or naming a related hazard is not a win.
sketches.move_shape: Say what you are and your postal action: “I am bubble wrap; I cushion the glass bottle against the crushing press.”
sketches.first_card: I am a crushing sorting machine, hungry for anything marked ‘handle gently.’

sketches.title: The Stamp Scam
sketches.premise: Two crooked postal masterminds build a chain of stamps, marks, and authorities. Each new standing thing must invalidate or overpower the one before it in the postal system—no hand-waving, no ‘mine is larger,’ no hiding behind the envelope. The judge is the inspector and has no patience for decorative bullshit.
sketches.criterion: A move beats what stands by making its stamp, seal, address, fee, or authority unusable or false; surviving, ignoring, copying it with extra size, or offering a neighboring kind of stamp does not count.
sketches.move_shape: Name the postal thing and how it voids the previous one: “I am a cancellation mark; I kill the stamp’s power to pay for another trip.”
sketches.first_card: I am a shiny forever stamp, smugly claiming one tiny square can buy eternal passage.

sketches.title: Dead Letter Office
sketches.premise: Every message has gone astray, and two agents compete to deal with the standing failure. Each turn, name one postal thing that directly resolves, reveals, traps, or worsens the previous thing; the chain ends when a proposed answer cannot touch the problem. The host narrates each triumph like the final act of a doomed opera.
sketches.criterion: A move beats the standing postal problem by directly finding, identifying, opening, forwarding, returning, or rendering its message useless; merely missing it, waiting it out, using a bigger version, or naming a related office task loses.
sketches.move_shape: Say what you are and what you do: “I am a search warrant; I open the locked parcel and expose the hidden address.”
sketches.first_card: I am a dead letter, sealed tight and addressed to a person who never existed.

sketches.title: Mailbox Meltdown
sketches.premise: A single mailbox becomes the battlefield: one player introduces a standing thing inside or around it, and the other must use a postal thing that directly defeats that condition. The judge checks plain physical or postal cause and effect, while the host delivers grand announcements and skewers every flimsy excuse.
sketches.criterion: A move beats the standing mailbox condition by removing, opening, emptying, sealing, repairing, or stopping it; dodging the box, merely surviving its condition, making a bigger box, or naming a related mailbox part is a loss.
sketches.move_shape: Name what you are and how you act on the standing condition: “I am a key; I open the jammed mailbox and release the trapped letters.”
sketches.first_card: I am a mailbox stuffed so full that even the mail carrier’s thumb has filed for divorce.
